newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end firmer but dampened by Lebed.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end firmer but dampened by Lebed.

text.p: Swiss shares ended marginally higher but failed to overcome the level of 3,800 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) in quiet trade and on moderate volumes.
News that Russian president Yeltsin sacked security chief Alexander Lebed pressured prices in the last half hour of the session. Dealers said U.S. economic data had little influence.
Dealers were unsure whether the SMI would overcome the 3,800 point level soon.
"It may be that U.S. economic data after the U.S. presidential elections will give rise to inflation fears", a dealer said.
SMI was up 0.08 percent, or 3.0 points, to 3,793.2.

Shares of UBS, CS Holding and utilities Electrowatt and Motor-Columbus were at first buoyed by news German electicity company Bayernwerk was interested in Electrowatt and Aare-Tessin AG fuer Elektrizitaet (Atel), dealers said.
But they fell back after late profit taking. UBS ended down one franc at 1,247.
CS Holding owns 44.9 percent of Electrowatt. UBS holds a majority stake in Motor-Columbus, which in turn owns more than 50 percent in Atel. The banks declined to comment on the alleged talks.
Sulzer up two francs to 762 after the company said it was going to cut 950 of 3,200 jobs at its weaving machine unit Sulzer Rueti.

One dealer said lower profit expectations for the Sulzer group may have led to some selling, bringing the share back down from 766 immediately after the job cut news. The stock had posted strong gains in the past few days.
Ciba and Sandoz saw renewed buying interest from U.S. and British investors after a recent weak streak, a dealer said.
Nestle was up one franc, possibly due to switches from Unilever, a trader noted. ABB rose six francs to 1,588.
